newsitem.title: USA: Reno orders probe into New York bombing plot.
newsitem.headline: Reno orders probe into New York bombing plot.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno has ordered an investigation to establish whether a suspect in an alleged New York bombing plot was allowed into the country after saying he had been detained in Israel for terrorism.

Reno said on Thursday she was looking into reports that one of the three men arrested, 23-year-old Gazi Ibrahim Abu Mezer, had filled out a U.S. immigration application in which he stated that he had been arrested previously in Israel "and accused of being a member of a known terrorist organisation."

Reno said she has ordered a complete chronology, and has asked the Federal Bureau of Investigation to work with the Immigration and Naturalisation Service and "see if there is anything that needs to be done to strengthen the appropriate exchange of information" between those agencies.
At her weekly news conference, Reno said the Justice Department's inspector general, its independent internal investigation arm, had also started a separate inquiry.
"I want to look to see what we need to do, if anything, to strengthen the process," she said. But she said it may not be possible to detect every potential danger at the border.

"One of the things that is clear is that with modern technology, with circumstances as they exist today, we may not be able to spot every one, and the most diligent of inspectors or border patrol agents may not be able to do with the facts at hand and the facts available to them to do it," she said.
Reno also said she has an "open mind" about a proposal to dismantle and split up the Immigration and Naturalisation Service. In the past the Justice Department had flatly opposed such suggestions.
A draft proposal from the U.S. Commission on Immigration Reform recommends splitting the INS into three parts. Final recommendations are expected in late September.

The Justice Department would keep control of U.S. borders and removing illegal immigration. The State Department would handle immigration services, including citizenship requests. And the Labour Department would address rules about foreign workers.
